rationale:
The two {test} items cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits`.

- **One entry per enclosing item.** In `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration`, `const B` holds two hits. The raw `results.matches` shows three hits (A once, B twice). The agent-facing page has exactly two entries, `n0` for A and `n1` for B. The `page["matches"]` assertion fixes this shape.
- **Entry contents.** The same assertion checks that each entry has exactly a `node` reference, one `excerpt` (a single string, even for the two-hit B), and a `tag`. The pagination test compares whole entries with `assert_eq!` against `{"node","excerpt","tag"}`. Extra or missing fields would fail.
- **Node reference lets the agent read the item.** `session.read_node` on the second match returns a `Dependency::Node` for the B declaration. So the reference resolves to the right item.
- **Tag accounts for use.** `finish_search` with `used: []` records no dependencies. With `used: ["2"]` it records the dependency for `code.rs#const[B]`.
- **Group before pagination, with page-local tags.** `search_pages_return_every_original_match_in_order` runs 350 lines, each containing two hits, so each item has several hits. It spans more than one page (`pages > 1`). Across pages it asserts these things:
  - Entries are consecutive, `n{count}`.
  - Each entry is the full line excerpt.
  - Tags restart at `index+1` on every page.
  - The total entry count equals the number of items (350, not 700 hits).
  - The source file is overwritten mid-run, so the pages come from the original snapshot.

  If grouping happened after pagination, an item could be split or duplicated across a page boundary. That would break the exact sequential node ids and the final count. I read `fn[chunks]` in `pages.rs` only to see what the pages are made of. It chunks the already-built entries by size, which agrees with the test's expectations.

I found no unacknowledged gap. Both tests carry {test} references to the subject.

The harness represents a domain `D::NodeId` to the agent as an opaque JSON string scoped to the conversation. It retains the IDs of the current node, supplied input nodes, and nodes introduced by tool results. Tools that return nodes give the agent references to those IDs. Tools that accept a node resolve its reference to the same ID. An unknown reference produces a tool error.
